title: Play and pause
one: The bookmark, a dark play inside it and a paper pause inside that.
idea: Your idea, cut as one paper shape: the bookmark, a dark play inside it and a paper pause inside the play. The play is A's shape, larger, and the pause has the proportions of the pause button in Shelf's player, so all three are Shelf's own.
built: The shared bookmark (base), unchanged, and A's construction (B's build imports A's). The play is the largest that leaves 6 dp of paper above it and along the notch: 36.62 × 28.29 dp, on A's axis (y 49.8), with 8.6 dp at the flat side and 8.2 past the drawn tip; its slanted edges are parallel to the notch, as A's are. The pause is the app's: Lucide's pause drawn filled at a 1.75 stroke, as the player shows it, has bars 2.56 times as wide as the gap and 3.09 times as tall as they are wide. Here the bars are 3.69 × 11.38 dp, 1.44 dp apart. The pause starts on the play's incircle (centre 50.83, 49.8, radius 9.96) and sits 1 dp left of it: there the dark is 4.55 dp along the flat side and 3.5 at the bars' outer corners, and because a band running parallel to a bar looks narrower than the same distance at a corner, the ring reads as even. The aim was 4.5 dp bars. With 6 dp walls 3.7 dp is the most that keeps the ring even (3.9 if the pause crowds the flat side). With the ring kept even, 4.5 dp bars need a play 42.3 dp tall, which leaves 3.2 dp of paper above it and along the notch (40.3 dp and 4.2 dp if the pause crowds the flat side): n3's outlined bookmark again.
corners: A's rule, matched by angle. The play's corners take the tail tips' radius (1.5/34 of the bookmark's width, 1.92 dp), since its back corners have the tips' 57 degree angle and its point is 66. Right angles take the shoulders' 4/34: 5.12 dp on the bookmark, and 4/34 of the bar's width on the pause (0.43 dp). The app's rounder bar ends (a third of the bar's width) were tried too: beside the crisp play they looked soft, so the shoulders' proportion stays. At 48 px the bars are square, on whole pixels.
small: 48 px keeps the pause at its smallest: bars 2 × 7 px with a 2 px gap on whole pixels (x 18 to 24, y 18 to 25), 3 px of dark at the flat side and 2.5 at the corners. The bars, the gap and that 2.5 px of dark at the corners (two pixels on the diagonal) are under this size's 3 px minimum, and the pause still reads as two bars, magnified and at 1x. A full 3 px at the corners needs 6 px bars in a play a pixel left of centre, which looked lopsided, or less than 3 px of paper above the play. At this size the gap is as wide as a bar, because the app's 2.5 to 1 would need 5 px bars. The play has to be 24.5 px tall, which leaves 3.3 px of paper above it and 3.4 along the notch, against the master's 6 dp (3.9 px at this scale); 9.1% soft. 32 px, 16 px and the glyph drop the pause, and B's files there are A's, byte for byte: at 32 px a play with 2 px walls holds 2 px bars with a 2 px ring only if the bars are 3 px tall, which reads as two dots; at 16 px there is no room; and the glyph sits beside the media notification's own play and pause. Without a pause, B's larger play would only thin the paper, so those sizes take A's play. Every cut uses base's bookmark unchanged.
risks: A play holding a pause is a media player's play/pause button, so this is the most player-like option and the nearest to Google Play Books, which pairs a play and a bookmark. The play takes 36.6 of the bookmark's 52 dp, so the paper is a 6 to 8.6 dp frame round it, the thinnest the judges would accept. The pause bars are 3.7 dp, under the 4.5 dp aim: on a 1x (48 px) home screen they are 2.5 px bars with a 1 px gap and merge into one small patch, while a Pixel's launcher draws about 2 px per dp, which makes them 7 px bars with a 3 px gap. The pause appears wherever the master is used (the launcher and its themed icon, both launch screens, and the mark on paper, as on the website) and in the 48 px cut; the 32 and 16 px cuts and the glyph are A's.
